tweets.text: Voting in a federal election without U.S. citizenship is a crime. Three noncitizens were convicted of illegal voting and related election offenses in federal court. Protecting the integrity of the electoral process and holding accountable those who violate federal election laws remains a top priority for our Office. Individuals who unlawfully register to vote or cast ballots in federal elections can face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and immigration consequences.

Graphic reading, "Three Noncitizens Convicted of Illegal Voting and Related Election Offenses in Federal Elections
Defendants Admitted to Voting in Federal Elections Despite Knowing They Were Not Eligible to Vote,
JUNE 22, 2026."

Graphic reading, “Voting in federal elections is one of the most important rights and responsibilities of American citizenship. Federal law is clear: 
only United States citizens 
may vote in federal elections. 
These defendants admitted that they knowingly violated that law. The Southern District of Florida is committed to protecting the integrity of our elections and ensuring that those who undermine public confidence in the electoral process are held accountable.”

-U.S. ATTORNEY JASON A. REDING QUINONES JUNE 22, 2026
